summary: The eval gate stopped failing for a reason unrelated to what it measures. Its near-miss corpus hardcoded an old trigger phrase, so when the trigger changed two of its cases quietly became real tags and the suite reported that the model had been invoked when it should not have been.
details: The corpus now states the matching RULES and is rendered against whatever trigger the deployment configures, so a trigger change - or a clone using a different name - cannot silently invalidate it.

Three config-template values that had fallen behind the deployment are reconciled: two are deliberate operator opt-ins and are now recorded as such with reasons, and the turn-token budget is synced because a separate invariant requires both files to agree on it.

Several tests built malformed configs by string replacement against a hardcoded trigger. Those replacements had silently become no-ops, so the tests were loading valid configuration while claiming to test invalid configuration.
limitations: Roughly 30 test files still name the old trigger as a self-contained fixture value. Those are cosmetic and were deliberately left alone; sweeping them mechanically changed the meaning of tests whose subject is the trigger shape itself.
